levels.name: Public
levels.definition: Already published, or written to be published. No harm if anyone sees it.

levels.name: Internal
levels.definition: The business's own working information. Mildly harmful if leaked; embarrassing, not damaging.
levels.may_leave_company: only to the party named in the document
levels.may_go_to_external_ai: only tools that do not retain data

levels.name: Client-confidential
levels.definition: Belongs to a client, or was shared by a client under a confidentiality clause. Leaking it damages the client and the relationship.
levels.approval_needed_to_share: owner, and the client where the contract says so

levels.name: Regulated
levels.definition: Personal data under the PDPA, financial account details, or health information. Mishandling is a legal matter, not just a commercial one.

regulated: phone number plus a person's name
client-confidential: a client's name plus a figure
words like unannounced, not public, keep quiet, NDA
a file whose header names a client

rule_of_thumb: When two levels could apply, the higher rank wins. A file is as sensitive as the most sensitive line in it.
